measurementNotes: Node 24-only within-runtime baseline/candidate comparisons. Earlier Node 22 protocols differ and are not matched cross-major performance controls.

Each long run keeps one session and one child generation through three stages covering 72 distinct source pages. At least 18 minutes include prompt execution, diagnostics and explicit pacing waits; this is not continuous CPU work or multi-hour leak evidence.

Old-generation and total heap peaks are child lifetime observational high-water marks including startup. Live-set lifetime peak is a post-major-GC upper bound, not current retained memory or a leak slope.

Stage and complete-workload GC deltas are computed within each PID/startticks generation. A stage without major GC has no live-set coverage; only the complete final workload requires positive major-GC coverage.

Tree RSS is a maximum sampled sum of daemon and observed descendants, including ACP and local MCP processes. Shared pages may be counted repeatedly; it is neither unique physical memory nor a continuous peak.
Per-turn context reports and event counts do not prove all delivered history remains resident or exhaustively observe compaction. Exact tool text is verified, but answer semantics are not graded.
MCP payloads are local repetitive synthetic text; registry/schema/server-log evidence does not establish capture of actual initial provider request schemas.

Resource tap and status/context diagnostics add overhead, which is included and not independently benchmarked. No forced GC or additional ACP resource polling is used. RPC IDs are matched internally but not serialized.
Capture ceilings remain 256 MiB samples, 32 MiB tool events and 16 MiB tap; instrumentation ceiling failures would be classified separately from product heap failures.

The second BA long pair spans batches with one preserved provider-error attempt between its arms; the retry is not hidden or pooled with partial turns. The Node 24 concurrent pair is a later fresh protocol that preserves the failed v4c attempt and captures only provider tool-schema summaries. These bounded pairs are not maximum deployment capacity, universal 544 MiB safety, or a statistically established latency/GC regression threshold.

The v5 experiment-only loopback proxy retained request metadata plus tool names and parameter-schema hashes. It did not retain authorization headers, message bodies, schema bodies or response bodies. Each arm had 36 provider requests; all 24 tool-bearing requests included read_file, none included tool_search, and no request failed to parse.
excluded: Startup-only preflights and provider readiness calls are not workload turns.

The original v4 run3 failed at turn 13 with zero tool calls after 12 successful turns/24 calls. Its answer was not archived, so the model reason is unknown. Failed-run audit passed 633 checks; this run and the five unstarted v4 jobs are excluded. v4b uses a new distinct-page protocol, not a completed original v4 matrix.

The second baseline in v4b failed at turn 22 with a model-serving internal error after 21 completed turns. Its partial workload is excluded; its complete baseline is retried once in a separate v4c batch using the identical v4b collector/protocol. Two concurrent jobs were unstarted in v4b and scheduled in v4c, but no Node 24 concurrent pair completed. The second BA pair therefore spans batches with a preserved failed attempt between arms.

The v4c concurrent/544 first wave failed: one session made two failed unregistered tool_search calls instead of its required read; the other three sessions each completed one exact read. All four end_turn events do not satisfy the workload contract. The baseline concurrent job was not started. All four workspace registry snapshots listed only read_file as enabled. The model claimed read_file was unavailable, but actual provider request schemas were not captured, so the cause remains unknown. This partial attempt stays excluded. The later v5 pair retries the workload with request-schema summaries and does not retroactively make v4c valid.
Earlier v1/v2/v2b/v3/v3b/v3c matrices retain separate provenance, including their failed attempts; none are pooled into these Node 24 accepted runs.
remaining: Broader real-world profiles, materially larger contexts, multi-hour stability and other host partitions remain open.
Define acceptable GC and latency thresholds plus staged rollout and rollback criteria before production heap enforcement.

decision.interpretation: The Node 24 long, MCP and four-child concurrent screens retain 544 MiB as a scope-specific candidate. They do not establish production admission readiness, a performance threshold, multi-hour stability or other host partitions.
